observation_summary: The compiler enters an infinite recursion (StackOverflowError) when processing recursive inheritance or interface implementation cycles, because the cycle detection logic was insufficient.
reasoning_summary: The fix involves changing the method called for cycle detection from 'detectImplicitPrototypeCycle' to 'detectInheritanceCycle'. This is a correction to the algorithmic strategy used to validate the inheritance graph, ensuring that cycles are correctly identified and handled before they cause infinite recursion. It is not a simple guard (Checking) or a value assignment, but a change in the procedural logic used to traverse and validate the type hierarchy.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix involves a conditional check, the core issue is the logic of the cycle detection algorithm itself, not just a missing guard.
The fix is a local procedural change to the type resolution algorithm, not a design-level capability correction.
